card.title: 102. GRENADIER
card.flavorText: During WWII, the 102nd Grenadier Regiment was part of the German 24th Infantry Division, alongside the 31st and 32nd Grenadier Regiments. The division was formed at Chemnitz in 1935 and first saw combat in Poland in 1939. It fought as part of 8th Army and suffered heavy losses in the fighting along the Bzura river, where Polish resistance hit the division hard. In 1940, the 24th Infantry Division took part in the campaign in France, notably the combat around Stonne. The next year it joined Army Group South for the invasion of the Soviet Union and fought in Ukraine, particularly the battles around Uman and Kiev. It then moved to Crimea under the 11th Army. During the final assault on Sevastopol in 1942, the division captured key positions, including Mekenziyevy Mountain station and Fort Stalin, but lost about 30 percent of its strength. Later in 1942, the division was sent north to the Leningrad sector. It was engaged in the difficult battles on the Volkhov Front, then retreated west during the Soviet offensives of 1944. It ended the war trapped in the Courland Pocket.
